author: KevineCove
body: "Walking as a bonus" is a really good microcosm of Orna. There are a few GPS based mechanics, namely Conqueror's Guild, memory hunts, and the Traveler's Guild. In theory you get the most stuff by maxing out at 10k steps every day, but in practice the rewards for doing this are situational and not something you'd usually want to do all the time. The Conqueror's Guild gives great rewards but realistically you won't get much unless you're playing from a vehicle.

author: timmahh112
body:
Yes, there'll be other activities and quests to actually seek out specific types of monsters that are area/terrain/biome specific.

In addition, as you start building your town, you'll get an Oracle Temple and go on memory hunts, and those require you to move and go into different locations and track down the memories.  These are pretty necessary.

You can get away without moving, but you'll be at a disadvantage and will be missing out on dungeons, raids, towers, etc.

author: Broad-Student8521
body:
When you walk around town you'll find more bosses and dungeons . Eventually you'll unlock towers and monuments . There is also the amity items that require you to use a item and walk around looking for the mini games to play.  

You can sit there and kill monsters for exp but after say lvl 75 that is a very slow way to level up . You will have to look for bosses/dungeons for exp

author: PlaysByBrulesRules
body:
Hey, I think for many players, a majority of the time spent is spent at home on the couch. 

However, the game absolutely does have systems which reward you for walking. At early levels, the best example of this may be finding dungeons or monuments to walk to so you can level up and get better gear. 

Dungeon locations will be fixed and the type of dungeon at each spot can rotate each week, while monuments (encountered around level 50 I think) give comparatively higher rewards and their locations change each week. So you have to search for them a bit.  

As you get further into the game, more and more game systems will become available to you, such as towers (think of these as special, harder monuments, and monuments are special kinds of dungeons that work a little differently). 

There are also a number of guilds in the game which offer rewards / progression for doing the different kinds of game activities. There is one called the traveler’s guild which explicitly centers on walking around. As you walk around you can charge up “aspects” which you can think of as little eggs that hatch monsters (“manifests”) from the game that you can put into your own personal Pokémon collection. Then you can use these manifests/monsters to complete challenges that give rewards. The travelers guild is actually one of the more under-utilized game mechanics but this month it received a big face lift and the Kingsfall event running now centers around it. So it’s getting newfound attention from the game devs.

Also every day you get rewards for walking 3k,6k and 10k steps, there’s a weekly 40k steps bonus. 

And the game has memory hunts which are kind of like little scavenger hunts that can require you to walk around and complete mini games. Memory hunts are arguably THE most powerful tool for maximizing your character progression once you have already reached T10 (level 225). But don’t worry about that for now :)

TLDR: if you prioritize level and power progression then this will not force you to walk around a lot per-se, but it is possible to choose your play style in a way that rewards you for walking a lot. 

I took a 45 minute walk today to get rewards in Orna, so it’s what you make of it

author: vitamin8080
body: Walking is the least efficient way to play this game. I first started playing this game for the gps walking and enjoyed leveling up and traveling to the PvE area guardians, but since they changed the system to the jank compass on menu system and removed rewards it killed all interest in the GPS aspect of the game. End game is pretty much max view distance gear and wayvesels.

author: r3dm0nk
body: It used to be a good gps game, now it's just another couch clicker.

author: Allalilacias
body:
Technically, yes, but, realistically, you get more out of using public transportation for it.

Like, I used to get a train and do a 50km route back and forth to play. I would sometimes get bored of playing for so long (I was already quite high level) and get out of the train and spend a few hours in some random town. I also used to take a bus to work and college and would play on both trips. It helped a lot.

I also knew a guy who used to send us pictures of the places he'd get to while walking. He didn't want to just walk, so he brought his phone to his walks. He'd do the same walk every day and would send pictures.

So you can do it, it's just not the most efficient way.

author: PathlessDemon
body:
I love this game for its simplicity, mechanics, and for helping me stay active.

I usually get my running and walking done, all thanks to the Traveller’s Guild.

author: permaculturegeek
body:
Some of the encouragement to travel (I won't say walk, actually I think cycling would be a great way to play, covering more ground) is quite subtle.
Say you have a quest to defeat 20 trolls. If you stay in one place just bopping mobs, you will get 3 or 4, but then their spawn rate will slow. If you move, though,vyou will often be rewarded with quest targets each new area you visit.
My walking is due to work, about 8km a day (big box retail), so I get the advantages of that in the game. Travellers is my second-highest guild.
Memory hunts are one of the encourage you to move features, but I used to hate them, because living rurally with a single road, I'd end up with all the points being inaccessible. They changed it to guarantee most points would spawn on a road, but I'm still not going to go out on a winter's night. So the "couchable if you've walked 10k steps" addition a couple of weeks ago is welcome.

author: abtbmx
body: you can do most things on this game right from the comfort of your home. the thing that you'll need to walk/drive for is conquering/exploring settlements and take then from other players. doing this grants tons of daily rewards like gold, orns and rare materials. then there are many other things you can access at higher tiers. Coliseums, specific dungeons, monuments, towers, alchemists and demonforges. also, some bosses spawn repeatedly in some locations for a period of time.
